extracted.intended_audience: prospective SageMath developers and contributors (new contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: A beginner-friendly developer guide describing how to prepare an environment, obtain the Sage source, use git and git-trac workflows, and follow project conventions to contribute code, documentation, translations, or tests to SageMath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to help / contribution types
rubrics_metrics.description: Everybody who uses Sage is encouraged to contribute something back to Sage at some point. How you can help: Add examples to the documentation; Find bugs or typos; Fix a bug; Implement a new function; Contribute a useful tutorial for a mathematical topic; Translate an existing document to a new language; Create a new class, create a fast new C library, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates the acceptable contribution types — documentation examples, bug reports/fixes, new functions or classes, tutorials, translations, C libraries, etc. Use the appropriate repository/workflow for the contribution type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the trac server for issue tracking and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Trac server account: used to create bug reports, discuss issues, propose changes, share code, …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign up for a trac account to file tickets, follow existing tickets, and collaborate. Many development workflows and ticket-centered branches rely on trac.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and maintain your own copy of the Sage source code
rubrics_metrics.description: Source code: You need your own copy of Sage’s source code to change it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clone the repository and work on local branches; do not edit the central repository directly. Use the develop branch as the base for ongoing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Sage conventions and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions and guidelines: document outlining Sage’s conventions and guidelines for code and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before contributing code or docs, read and adhere to the project's conventions (coding style, documentation rules, tests). The guide points to a dedicated document for these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use git for revision control and sharing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Git: To share changes with the Sage community, you will need to learn about revision control; here is a git cheat sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contributions should be managed via git. Learn basic git commands (branching, committing, pushing, pulling) and follow repository branch conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic git workflow for making and sharing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: git workflow: configure git and obtain the source code … create or download a branch: git branch / git clone URL; make changes: edit; rebuild; test; save (git commit); share changes: git push / git pull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical steps: create or checkout a branch (preferably based on develop), edit code, rebuild Sage or run tests, commit locally, then push to share. Use descriptive branch names and commit messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: git-trac workflow for ticket-oriented development
rubrics_metrics.description: git-trac workflow: configure git, obtain the source code, configure git-trac … create or checkout a ticket: git trac create 'fix bug in Sage' / git trac checkout TICKETNUMBER; make changes: edit; rebuild (sage -br); test; share changes: git commit; git trac push [TICKETNUMBER]; git trac pull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use git-trac commands to create/checkout ticket branches tied to trac tickets. Rebuild with sage -br when appropriate. Use git trac push to publish ticket branches and git trac pull to fetch updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign up for a trac account with required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Ready 1: Sign up for a trac account — Send an email to sage-trac-account@googlegroups.com with: your full name, preferred username, contact email and reason for needing a trac account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the listed fields in the request email; the trac account is required for ticket creation and SSH key linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate and link SSH keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Ready 2: Generate SSH keys for your computer: ssh-keygen. Link your SSH keys with your trac account: Log in to trac, click Preferences, go to SSH Keys tab, paste the content of your public key file (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub) and Save changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must do this once per computer you will use for development (including CoCalc projects). Linking SSH keys enables authenticated pushes and other operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install and configure git and git-trac
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Ready 3: Configure git and git-trac — install and configure git: git config --global user.name "Your Name"; git config --global user.email you@yourdomain.example.com. Install git-trac: git clone https://github.com/sagemath/git-trac-command.git; cd git-trac-command; python setup.py install. Configure git-trac: git trac config --user username --pass password.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set your git identity, install the git-trac helper, and configure it with your trac credentials so you can use git-trac commands seamlessly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get the Sage source and build a working developer copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Ready 4: Get the Sage source code — git clone git@trac.sagemath.org:sage.git; cd sage; git checkout develop. Build Sage: make start (this command will build Sage and test that Sage starts, but it will not build the documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the develop branch for development. make start builds Sage enough to run; building the whole project (including docs) may require more steps. While Sage builds, explore trac for tickets to work on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Reviewer’s checklist / review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the review process: See also the Reviewer’s check list in the Sage Developer’s Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing or preparing contributions, follow the project's reviewer checklist to ensure consistent quality and that required checks/tests are present. The page references the checklist rather than reproducing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long recompiles when checking out old ticket branches (tip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips and Tricks: Checkout an old ticket without recompiling for hours — if you checkout the branch associated with a ticket using git trac checkout TICKETNUMBER then your version of Sage will coincide with the version of Sage on which the branch is based and make build will compile an older version of Sage which can take a very long time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, merge the branch with the most recent version of develop: git checkout develop; git checkout -b t/TICKETNUMBER/TICKETNAME; git trac fetch TICKETNUMBER; git merge FETCH_HEAD; [git trac push]. This updates the branch to the latest development version and avoids building an old baseline; resolve conflicts if necessary and optionally push the updated branch.
